paper.title_en: Phenomenology of the Vector-like Lepton Model for Lepton-flavour Violating Observables
paper.abstract_en:
Charged lepton flavour violation (cLFV) is a clear sign of physics beyond the Standard Model
(SM) and has not yet been observed experimentally. Future experiments like Mu2e or COMET
aim to improve the sensitivity to cLFV observables by several orders of magnitude, sparking
interest in models which can generate experimentally accessible branching ratios for such ob
servables. The class of vector-like lepton (VLL) models, extending the SM by one or more gen
erations of vector-like lepton multiplets, is able to generate experimentally accessible branching
ratios for cLFV observables. This thesis analyzes in detail the parameter space of one par
ticular VLL model, which extends the SM by a VLL singlet and doublet. The focus is laid
upon cLFV observables, such as muon conversions in nuclei and muon decays to electrons
and photons. It is shown that this VLL model has wide and consistent parameter spaces in
which cLFV observables can be generated by various different mechanisms and contributions,
that go beyond what would be expected in models with dipole dominance. Various different
dominance and clustering regimes are identified, demonstrating the versatility of the model’s
parameter space. It is furthermore shown that the parameter space allows for experimentally
accessible branching ratios for muon conversions in nuclei as well as muon decays to electrons
and photons, while still being consistent with all other experimental constraints, without the
need for large finetuning or strongly hierarchical couplings.
